scenes.say: This branch took a hit.
People left. The work didn't.
Nothing here fell over.
The month it happened, we closed two hundred and four requests. This month, two hundred and forty.
So before Friday, look at who's still standing.
Nineteen agents. Two managers. And five behind them: three in support, the branch manager's assistant, and our driver. Not one of them has left.
Between us, two hundred and twenty-one years of this work.
Put us all on one line and it runs from nineteen ninety-three to this year.

Eighty-seven agents have come through this branch in the sixteen years the record covers. Fifty-one resigned. There were four retirements, three left vested, and two transferred inside Guardian. And in all that time, two terminations.

When this company launched its first digital application, with a digital signature on it, this branch led the team that built it. We didn't go digital this year. Our first digital submission was filed in two thousand and eleven.
We don't do AI for the sake of it. We use it to make what we already have far more robust.
Start with the fact find. On the first of August, it went live again. Rebuilt from the ground up.
And we put the order right. You meet your client. You send the draft. Your client approves it. Only then does it reach a manager.

A hundred and forty-four fact finds this year, sixty-three already through a manager, and one in five came back for more work. The training runs every week, and agents who started this on paper are turning out full recommendations now.
And since the digital fact find went live, not one of those cases has lapsed.

Here's the part nobody talks about: all of this protects you. Market conduct, clause by clause, and our fact find answers every one. Fraud is rising across this industry. Early detection is the job of a proper fact find, and the surveys told us why people pushed back.
We don't treat a client as a transaction. We build a journey. Onboarding. The birthday. A premium due. A requirement. A review every six months.
And this branch took something on by itself that most of you never heard about. Nearly three thousand letters and reminders. Three hundred and forty-nine files opened.
You are equipped. Query Pal answers a client any hour of the day. Your clients sign in themselves. Every tool behind one sign-in.
The system sets your day before you're even up.
The paper moved too. We scrapped the old form and built the transmittal ourselves. Three thousand six hundred papers, and three quarters reached Guardian inside a working day.
In the last twelve months, this team closed two thousand four hundred and ninety-five requests.
Production, goals, pendings, the transmittal — live on the walls in here all day, and on the wall outside where everybody walks past. What's done, what's late, and whose name is on it.
scenes.screen: THE WALLS, LIVE IN THE BRANCH

scenes.say: We have the lowest lapse rate of any branch in this company. Ours is four point nine six per cent. The average across the main branches is eight point eight two.
Sixty-seven per cent of our agents are still here a year later. The published average is between fifty-five and sixty.

I've been in this business thirty-five years. The only way you guide people and still scale is to put everything you know where everybody can reach it. That is the promise Akaash and I have made to you.

And there is a way up from here. Agent. Executive Agent. Trainee Manager. Unit Manager. This branch grows its own. And the three-year plan runs to September twenty twenty-nine: rebuild the bench, grow the units, forty agents.
The cracks are still there. We didn't hide them. They're part of the shield now.
We're not going back to what this branch was. We're going somewhere better.
Friday, twelve noon, ninety minutes. Seventy-five of them belong to you, not to me.
Three questions are already waiting for you. Answer one tonight.
Sign in on Friday with your agent number. Signing in is the register. Guests use the visitor code: zero, zero, zero, zero.
We rise together.
